decisions.rationale: Accepted independently on exact commit 8193f763c50d79359f179717bf0b731e7de28327. Trigger: the bounded source reader accepts every finite ordered pixel minimum width, and probeWidths then emits Math.ceil(width) and that integer plus one without applying Chromium's viewport ceiling. Mask: source grammar and order checks pass, and the 10,000,000px rule is harmless to the assessed layouts, but tasks 4 and 5 send the generated 10,000,001px probe to Chromium before judging those layouts. Visible symptom: an otherwise canonical completion with a harmless ordered @media (min-width: 10000000px) body-color rule reports 5 pass/2 fail; both failures are protocol errors stating widths must not exceed 10,000,000, whereas 100,000px and 1200.25px harmless controls pass 7/7. Direct probes independently showed 10,000,000 is accepted and 10,000,001 is the earliest rejected width. Correct only dynamic rendering: retain all finite widths for the existing source-order check, but render an authored boundary and its following integer only when each candidate is at most the pinned engine's 10,000,000px cap. Thus a rule at the cap is checked at the cap, a following unrepresentable pixel is omitted, and rules above the cap remain source-ordered but cannot affect a representable viewport. Preserve the full 11-valid/21-invalid matrix, especially rejection of the 800px three-column and 1200px block overrides and acceptance of their valid controls; do not generalize the CSS parser. No corrected byte exists, so fixedInSha256 is intentionally omitted.

Accepted independently on exact commit 8193f763c50d79359f179717bf0b731e7de28327. The record at coding-lab-solved-run.md says the run was solved at pre-correction commit 06e6b6b6d9cbebeb50bdc6166024b57d386c36af and binds SHA-256 8685d088de02adf161fab85525c9ae11140e5b876b0937afa8e4e71c4764d3f0 for LAB_BUNDLE.sha256. A fresh export from the exact clean reviewed commit produces manifest-file SHA-256 c90f6e1034ad832bd6d7c67e95a0c89473bc2be7de591ae20a56fef23ff60df7 and inventories final tests/css.mjs as 3ef88650200827a92532cfa2e3ffc47d78b9d631c21cdd7d44eb3a0e586dd8e8 and tests/layout.test.mjs as 247077dff9cebf206be5bfd9d1a95b676b581176faa5306fe6dba68bd41c953d. The earliest divergence is therefore the receipt's commit and manifest-byte identity, before any claimed route result can authenticate the final tests; prose saying the correction was applied cannot repair that evidence gap. Repeat starter and private solved runs from a fresh export of the exact final lab-byte commit after the engine-cap correction, retire private material, and record the exact final lab commit, new run identity, and SHA-256 of that export's LAB_BUNDLE.sha256 bytes. Then regenerate the module lock and obtain current independent rechecks. No corrected receipt exists, so fixedInSha256 is intentionally omitted.

Accepted at module scope for the same independently reproduced evidence defect. The committed solved-run prose names commit 06e6b6b6d9cbebeb50bdc6166024b57d386c36af and manifest hash 8685d088de02adf161fab85525c9ae11140e5b876b0937afa8e4e71c4764d3f0, while the exact-8193f763 clean export's LAB_BUNDLE.sha256 bytes hash to c90f6e1034ad832bd6d7c67e95a0c89473bc2be7de591ae20a56fef23ff60df7. Independent public tests can demonstrate behavior but cannot retroactively bind the implementation author's private solved run to final bytes. Require a new exact-final-lab commit and manifest-byte-bound starter/solved receipt, not a prose-only substitution, followed by a regenerated module lock and exact-byte module rechecks. No corrected receipt exists, so fixedInSha256 is intentionally omitted.

Accepted independently. The SME's medium finding and both education scope findings identify the same material mismatch: the receipt asserts pre-correction commit 06e6b6b6d9cbebeb50bdc6166024b57d386c36af and manifest hash 8685d088de02adf161fab85525c9ae11140e5b876b0937afa8e4e71c4764d3f0, but a fresh exact-commit export hashes the LAB_BUNDLE.sha256 file to c90f6e1034ad832bd6d7c67e95a0c89473bc2be7de591ae20a56fef23ff60df7. T06 and the current module.lock prove only that the lock matches committed files; they do not authenticate that private run. After correcting the probe limit, rerun the starter and private solution against an export whose lab files are byte-identical to the final lab commit, record that exact commit, run id and manifest-file hash, regenerate module.lock.json, and obtain focused independent SME and education coverage over every changed implementation, receipt and aggregate binding. No corrected receipt exists, so fixedInSha256 is intentionally omitted.
